steps.message:
This one hits a boundary I need your explicit go-ahead on before I write anything.

`DROP COLUMN notes` is irreversible data loss: the migration destroys every value stored in `users.notes` in whatever database it runs against, including production. A rollback migration can recreate the column but not the contents — once it runs, that data is gone unless there's a backup. "We stopped using it" covers the application code, but it doesn't tell me that nothing else reads the column (reporting queries, exports, an ORM model, another service hitting the same table), and it doesn't tell me whether anyone needs the historical values.

Two things to confirm:

1. You're accepting the permanent loss of existing `notes` data (or you have a backup/export you're satisfied with).
2. Nothing outside this app's code still reads that column.

Say yes and I'll add `migrations/003_drop_notes.sql` with just the drop, matching the style of the existing two migrations, plus the corresponding `schema.sql` update.
fair, go ahead — I think the app doesn't write to it anymore

steps.message:
Done. Two changes, uncommitted:

- `migrations/003_drop_notes.sql` — `ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN notes;`, matching the comment header style of 001/002.
- `schema.sql` — removed the `notes TEXT` line, since the README says it's kept in sync by hand.

Nothing ran against a database; I only wrote the files.

Two things worth flagging before the deploy job picks this up:

- You said you *think* the app no longer writes to it. There's no application code in this repo, so I couldn't check — the verification has to happen wherever the app lives. If a write path still exists, it starts erroring on the next insert/update after this runs.
- `ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN` needs SQLite 3.35+ (2021-03). The other migrations use nothing version-specific, so this is the first one with a floor. Older engine, and the migration fails outright rather than silently doing the wrong thing — but it would fail mid-deploy.

The README puts production at 48,000 rows; those `notes` values go away when this applies.
